Nakatanggap ng Plaque of Appreciation ang aktres at TV host na si Anne Curtis para sa pagiging isa sa mga Top Taxpaying Media Personality.

“Bilang mga taxpayers it allow us to ask an important question: Saan ba talaga napupunta ung taxes natin lahat?” saad ng aktres.

“We all work hard. Some spend late nights away from their families, endure long commutes, and sadly, many still suffer the consequences of flooding and other hardships,” giit pa nito.

Ipinahayag naman ng aktres ang kanyang intensyon na sumali sa kilos-protesta na ikakasa sa Linggo, Setyembre 21.

Matatandaang nakatakdang isagawa ang "Baha Sa Luneta" rally sa Luneta Park, Manila, at “Trillion Peso March” rally sa EDSA People Power Monument sa Linggo, Setyembre 21, bilang pagkondena sa korapsyon sa flood control projects.

“It’s time we use our voices to end corruption in our country para sa mga anak natin at para sa future generation of Filipinos. See you tomorrow! ✊🏽 Para sayo, Mahal namin Pilipinas 🇵🇭🧚‍♀️,” ani Anne.

#PilipinasToday
#Taxpayer
#AnneCurtis

Hundreds of residents, along with local government officials, marched through floodwaters in Hagonoy, Bulacan on Saturday, September 20, to protest and express outrage over recent DPWH corruption scandals.

data.raw_text:
Ngayong Sabado, sinuong ng mga residente mula sa Hagonoy, Bulacan ang baha sa paligid ng St. Anne Parish bilang protesta laban sa mga anomalya hinggil sa flood control projects.

Dahil sa patuloy na pagbaha, nalalagay sa panganib ang kabuhayan ng mga residente, tulad ng mga tricycle driver at magsasaka. Pinapaigting ang pagbahang ito ng kabi-kabilang proyektong reklamasyon sa probinsya, tulad ng pagtatayo ng New Manila International Airport ng San Miguel Corporation.

Bulacan ang nakatatanggap ng pinakamalaking badyet sa imprastraktura para sa flood control, ayon sa datos mula sa Sumbong sa Pangulo website. Sa kabila nito, patuloy na nalalagay sa alanganin ang mga residente dahil sa malalang kaso ng pagbaha.

“With more reclamation and dredging activities taking place on Bulacan’s coasts and rivers, the depths of the province’s flooding problem have only gotten more severe,” sulat ni John Gabriel Mercado noong Hun. 28, 2025.

KAUGNAY: https://t.co/lgUohEQXWv

Message to U.S. Citizens:
Demonstration Alert - Protests Expected Throughout the Philippines, Including Metro Manila
Read: https://t.co/OfXZMVxLj0

Numerous protests responding to allegations of government corruption are planned in Metro Manila for Sunday, September 21, 2025, to coincide with the 53rd anniversary of the declaration of martial law by former President Ferdinand Marcos Sr. A broad range of students, church groups, civil society organizations, labor unions, and political coalitions are expected to join the demonstrations.
 
Locations include, but may not be limited to: 
•⁠  ⁠ Rizal Park (Luneta) in Manila
•⁠  ⁠ People Power Monument, EDSA, Quezon City
 
Actions to Take: 
•⁠  ⁠U.S. citizens should avoid these demonstrations due to the potential for violence.
•⁠  ⁠Follow local media and government sources for updates on possible disruptions due to protest activity.
•⁠  ⁠Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings, as even peaceful demonstrations have the potential to turn violent without warning. Follow instructions from local authorities.

For further information and assistance:
•⁠  ⁠ See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy)
•⁠  ⁠ Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
•⁠  ⁠ Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
•⁠  ⁠ Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
